title: Sexual and reproductive health and rights: infographic snapshot: Kuwait 2021

sections.title: Page 1

summary.text: Introduces a 2021 infographic snapshot of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in Kuwait, explaining that it summarises national data across the life course to help set priorities and plan programmes. It notes the data come from international sources and that intersectionality and non-binary gender categories are poorly captured.

sections.extract: This country snapshot provides an overview of national data relating to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) throughout the life course. Realization of SRHR requires provision of comprehensive, people-centred services, that address the different elements of SRHR, and which are supported by an enabling environment, quality health systems, and meaningful community engagement. Multiple, synergistic

sections.title: Page 2

summary.text: Presents demographic, sexual and reproductive health and HIV data for Kuwait, including a population of 4.3 million, life expectancy, a fertility rate of 2.1, a low adolescent birth rate and neonatal mortality of 4.5 per 1000 live births. Most HIV indicators are marked as having no data, and a context note links SRHR to the SDGs and universal health coverage.

sections.title: Page 3

summary.text: Summarises Kuwait's laws and policies affecting SRHR, showing for example that HIV transmission is criminalized, entry for people with HIV is restricted, PrEP is available but self-testing is not allowed. It also records that abortion is allowed only to save a woman's life or for foetal impairment, spousal consent is required for married women's SRH services, and same-sex behaviour, sex work and drug offences carry punitive laws.

sections.title: Page 4

summary.text: Presents health system indicators for Kuwait, including a UHC service coverage index of 76, legislation on universal health coverage, health workforce density and health spending of 5% of GDP. It notes no condom stock-outs and both paper and electronic health information systems, while several indicators lack data.

sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: Presents reproductive health service indicators for Kuwait, where nearly all births are attended by skilled personnel but most contraception, antenatal care, HIV and syphilis testing and abortion indicators have no data. A note stresses women's right to choose whether and when to have children and to access quality reproductive care.

sections.title: Page 6

summary.text: Presents sexual health service indicators for Kuwait, showing most HIV prevention and treatment cascade data are missing, 41 current PrEP users, and services for survivors of rape such as emergency contraception and post-exposure prophylaxis. It records no national HPV vaccination or cervical cancer screening programme.

sections.title: Page 8

summary.text: The first page of endnotes for the Kuwait SRHR snapshot, noting the April 2021 data cutoff and giving the year and source of each indicator, mainly UN population data, WHO and UNFPA publications and DHS surveys, with many marked as no data.

sections.extract: The cutoff for data included in this Infographic Snapshot is 15/04/2021. The year provided for each endnote is the date of the latest available data with an earliest date of 2011. Where data is not available in an international data source ‘No data’ is stated. This does not mean that no data exists for this indicator but that no data was found in internationally validated data sources. 1. Starrs, A. M. et al (2018)
